title: Overrides that narrow a window

blocks.text: Riverbend Water (invented for this practice) lets its engineers narrow when a main replacement may start. Each project has a start window, a `range` of years, and one start variable $`x_t \in \{0,1\}`$ per year $`t`$ of the window, with bounds $`l_t \le x_t \le u_t`$. Three kinds of override exist:

items: `start_in`, with `years = (y,)`: the project starts in year $`y`$.
`only_between`, with `years = (a, b)`: the project may start only from $`a`$ to $`b`$, both included; it does not have to start at all.
`skip_years`, with any number of years: the project may not start in those years (a road is closed, a festival needs the street); it does not have to start at all.

blocks.text: Write `bounds_for(kind, years, window)` in `overrides.py`. It returns `{t: (l_t, u_t)}` for every year `t` of the window, with `(0, 1)` for a year the override leaves free. An override that would set every year of the window to `(0, 0)` would quietly take the project out of the plan, which is not what was asked: return `None` for it instead, so the service can refuse it. A `start_in` year outside the window falls under that rule too. A `kind` that is none of the three narrows nothing: every year of the window gets `(0, 1)`. About twelve lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from overrides import bounds_for

window = range(2033, 2037)   # 2033 to 2036

print("start_in 2035:", bounds_for("start_in", (2035,), window))
print("only_between 2034-2035:", bounds_for("only_between", (2034, 2035), window))
print("skip_years 2033, 2036:", bounds_for("skip_years", (2033, 2036), window))
print("only_between 2040-2041:", bounds_for("only_between", (2040, 2041), window))

cases.says: start_in fixes its year at 1 and every other year of the window at 0
only_between leaves both of its end years free
skip_years closes the named years and leaves the others free, not forced
an override that closes every year of the window is refused with None

origin.section: An Override Is a Request, Checked Against the Data Before Any Bound Moves

concepts: each kind of override sets the lower and upper bounds of the project's start variables
an override that would close every start year is refused before any bound moves
